title: Finding primary research
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of finding primary research
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: A record reporting its own study
A summary or interpretation of another source

blocks.text: A blog says experiment had100 cases; original methods say40 and supplementary version says60 after revision.
Track versions and use the correct original record for the claim. The blog is secondary; the two original versions must not be merged silently.

Compare the intermediate evidence with the final statement. Explain why each number or decision follows from the stated inputs. The conclusion belongs to this scenario and procedure; changing the inputs, evaluation population or authority can change what it establishes. Retain the raw record so a later revision can be compared honestly.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case
guided_practice.prompt: A blog says experiment had100 cases; original methods say40 and supplementary version says60 after revision. Show the intermediate steps and give the conclusion with its scope.
guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Track versions and use the correct original record for the claim. The blog is secondary; the two original versions must not be merged silently.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: A search result describes a benchmark score, but the linked paper uses a different dataset. What should the comparison record contain?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Exact paper/version, dataset, metric and reported result; mark the search-summary mismatch rather than borrowing its number.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Being primary does not guarantee soundness; methods and evidence still require assessment.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: Record title, authors, version, date, identifier and access location. Distinguish paper, code, data and commentary. Verify that a quoted claim belongs to the cited version.

blocks.text: Before applying the procedure, write its units, denominator or decision boundary where relevant. A partner should be able to repeat each step using the same inputs. If a required input is absent or violates the stated contract, record that condition explicitly instead of quietly replacing it with a convenient value.
Connect the picture and the explanation
Point to the input, the deciding step and the result in this week’s visual. Explain the same step in ordinary words. A picture helps when you can say what each part represents.
